description: A game of snake whose position, direction, length and collisions are all available as control voltage and gates

params.text: Sets how many columns wide the screen is, 3 to 64
Sets how many rows tall the screen is, 3 to 32
Switches the edges of the screen between solid walls that end the game and open edges the snake passes through
Steers the snake upwards, if it is not already travelling down
Steers the snake to the right, if it is not already travelling left
Steers the snake downwards, if it is not already travelling up
Steers the snake to the left, if it is not already travelling right

inputs.text: The clock: the game moves one frame on each rising edge
Sets the column a new piece of food appears in, 0-10V across the width of the screen; with nothing patched the column is random
Sets the row a new piece of food appears in, 0-10V from the top of the screen to the bottom; with nothing patched the row is random
A rising edge steers the snake upwards, if it is not already travelling down
A rising edge steers the snake to the right, if it is not already travelling left
A rising edge steers the snake downwards, if it is not already travelling up
A rising edge steers the snake to the left, if it is not already travelling right
A rising edge puts a new piece of food on the screen

outputs.text: How far to the snake's left the nearest wall or piece of its own body lies, 0-10V across the screen
How far ahead of the snake's head the nearest wall or piece of its own body lies, 0-10V across the screen
How far to the snake's right the nearest wall or piece of its own body lies, 0-10V across the screen
A gate that is high for the frame in which the snake eats a piece of food
The column the food is in, 0-10V across the width of the screen
The row the food is in, 0-10V from the top of the screen to the bottom
Which way the snake is travelling: 0V up, 2.5V right, 5V down, 7.5V left
The column the snake's head is in, 0-10V across the width of the screen
The row the snake's head is in, 0-10V from the top of the screen to the bottom
How long the snake is, 0-10V against the number of cells on the whole screen
The column the snake's last segment is in, 0-10V across the width of the screen
The row the snake's last segment is in, 0-10V from the top of the screen to the bottom
A gate that goes high when the game is over and low again when the next game starts
Where along the top edge the snake last crossed or struck, 0-10V
Where along the right edge the snake last crossed or struck, 0-10V
Where along the bottom edge the snake last crossed or struck, 0-10V
Where along the left edge the snake last crossed or struck, 0-10V
A gate that is high for the frame in which the snake crosses or strikes the top edge
A gate that is high for the frame in which the snake crosses or strikes the right edge
A gate that is high for the frame in which the snake crosses or strikes the bottom edge
A gate that is high for the frame in which the snake crosses or strikes the left edge

notes: nothing happens until a clock is patched to the input at the centre of the direction buttons; the game moves one frame per rising edge.
with the mouse over the panel the arrow keys or W, A, S and D steer the snake.
the width and height knobs resize the screen while a game is running, which can leave the snake outside it.
menu: start length — how many segments long the snake is at the start of a game
steps to wait after game over — how many clock steps pass between the game ending and the next one starting
< bouncer — turns the snake along the wall instead of ending the game when it would hit one
= lock snake length — keeps the snake the length it started at, whatever it eats
@ leave trail — leaves the path the snake has taken drawn on the screen
% relative turning — makes the four direction controls turn left and right from where the snake is heading rather than pointing at a compass direction
$ ghost snake — lets the snake pass through walls and through itself without dying
? random start row — starts each game on a random row rather than the bottom one
_ don't eat food — leaves the food where it is when the snake crosses it
* multiple foods — allows more than one piece of food on the screen at a time
+ keep foods (needs *) — leaves earlier pieces of food on the screen instead of clearing them
# show grid — draws the cell grid on the screen
